title: Finite-coefficient evaluation of the quotient-diagram projection mate
statement:
Let $A$ be a commutative Noetherian ring, $I\subset A$ an ideal, $A_n=A/I^n$ for $n\ge1$, and $u:\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal X)\to\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal Y)$ a morphism of topoi presented by sites small in the module universe [def-weil-size-convention, def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. Write $D_T=D(\operatorname{Mod}(\underline A_T))$ for the ordinary unbounded module derived categories [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf, def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category], $u^*\dashv P=Ru_*$ for the canonical derived adjunction, with counit $\varepsilon$ and ordinary derived tensor [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-projection-mate-exact]. Put $J=\mathbf N_{\ge1}^{\mathrm{op}}$ and use the small diagram sites of [lem-weil-pbc-diagram-site-realization]. Their constant ring sheaves are $\Delta\underline A_T$ and their quotient ring sheaves are $B_T=(\underline{A_n}_T)_n$ with the actual quotient transitions. A $B_T$-module system consists of module sheaves $M_n$ over $\underline{A_n}_T$ and $\underline{A_{n+1}}_T$-linear transition maps to $M_n$ by restriction of scalars. Write $U_T$ for restriction to constant-$A$ towers, $S_T=-\otimes^L_{\Delta\underline A_T}B_T$, $\mathcal R_T=S_T\Delta$, and $i_V:\Delta V\to U_T\mathcal R_TV$ for the quotient augmentation. Write $G=u^*$ termwise, $P^J=Ru_*^J$ for derived termwise direct image on constant-$A$ towers, $G_B\dashv P_B$ for the quotient-ring diagram adjunction, and $\mathcal L_T=R\lim$ on constant-$A$ towers [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit]. All derived adjunctions are the ones induced from the module adjunctions, not separately chosen hom-set bijections. Use the canonical scalar-extension tensor comparisons of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback]. For arbitrary $H\in D_{\mathcal X}$ and $K\in D_{\mathcal Y}$ put $M=PH\otimes_A^LK$ and $N=H\otimes_A^Lu^*K$. Let $h_H:\mathcal R_{\mathcal Y}PH\to P_B\mathcal R_{\mathcal X}H$ be the coefficient mate with transpose $S_{\mathcal X}\Delta(\varepsilon_H)$. Let $\pi_B$ be the counit-defined projection for $G_B\dashv P_B$. The scalar-extension identifications
$$\mathcal R_{\mathcal Y}M\cong\mathcal R_{\mathcal Y}PH\otimes_{B_{\mathcal Y}}^L\mathcal R_{\mathcal Y}K,\qquad\mathcal R_{\mathcal X}N\cong\mathcal R_{\mathcal X}H\otimes_{B_{\mathcal X}}^LG_B\mathcal R_{\mathcal Y}K$$
define the single quotient-diagram arrow $v=\pi_B(h_H\otimes1):\mathcal R_{\mathcal Y}M\to P_B\mathcal R_{\mathcal X}N$. Put $H_n=H\otimes_A^L\underline{A_n}$, $K_n=K\otimes_A^L\underline{A_n}$ and let $u_n^*\dashv Ru_{*,A_n}$ be the ordinary quotient-coefficient adjunction. Exact evaluation and the derived restriction/direct-image comparisons identify the evaluation of this arrow with
$$\operatorname{ev}_n(v)=\pi^{(n)}_{H_n,K_n}(h_{H,n}\otimes_{A_n}^L1_{K_n}),$$
where $h_{H,n}:(PH)_n\to Ru_{*,A_n}H_n$ is the evaluated coefficient mate and $\pi^{(n)}$ is the adjunct of the quotient counit tensored with identity. The source is balanced as $M_n\cong(PH)_n\otimes_{A_n}^LK_n$ and the target as $Ru_{*,A_n}(H_n\otimes_{A_n}^Lu_n^*K_n)$. The evaluation comparisons carry the diagram adjunction to this specified finite adjunction, including its counit. The identifications are natural and compatible with quotient transitions. No preservation of K-injectives by varying-ring evaluation, perfectness, completeness or flatness of the quotients is assumed.

proof.text: Realize the quotient ring system as a ring sheaf on the sequence site using [lem-pur-system-ringed-sequence-site]. The equivalence identifies module maps with the specified semilinear transitions. By [lem-pur-system-level-left-extension], its derived evaluations $e_n^T$ are exact and have derived left adjoints $L_n^T$, with $e_m^TL_n^TP=B_{T,m}\otimes^L_{B_{T,n}}P$ for $m\leq n$ and zero for $m>n$. These are adjunctions of strict-system derived categories. In particular $e_n^TL_n^T\cong1$, with the multiplication identification. Evaluation is also a ringed inverse image with identity coefficient map [lem-pur-system-evaluation-topos]; hence its derived tensor comparison is the canonical one of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-projection-mate-exact] to the ringed diagram topoi to obtain the specified $G_B\dashv P_B$ and its counit $\varepsilon^B$.

source.place: Tags 07A4 (lemma-pullback-tensor-product), 07A6 (lemma-adjoint), 0D6E (lemma-derived-pushforward-composition), and 0B56 (equation-projection-formula-map); evaluation argument uses Zheng Construction 4.1, printed p. 21.

proof.text:
There is a canonical comparison $c_n:G_BL_n^{\mathcal Y}\xrightarrow{\sim}L_n^{\mathcal X}u_n^*$. Construct it on the actual singleton extensions, not merely on their evaluated objects. For a flat-term K-flat $B_{\mathcal Y,n}$-complex $Q$, [lem-pur-system-single-derived-extension] computes $L_nQ$ by its ordinary singleton extension. At $m\leq n$ the comparison is the tensor pullback map
$$u_m^*(B_{\mathcal Y,m}\otimes_{B_{\mathcal Y,n}}Q)\cong B_{\mathcal X,m}\otimes_{B_{\mathcal X,n}}u_n^*Q;$$
at $m>n$ it is the identity of zero. These maps commute with transitions: on a local tensor $b\otimes q$, either order applies the quotient map to $b$ and inverse image to $q$. This is the ordinary extension of [lem-pur-system-ordinary-single-extension]. It is a K-flat complex with flat terms over $B_{\mathcal Y}$: each level $B_{\mathcal Y,m}\otimes_{B_{\mathcal Y,n}}Q$ is K-flat with flat terms over $B_{\mathcal Y,m}$ by [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-pullback-preserves-kflat] for the identity topos with ring map $B_{\mathcal Y,n}\to B_{\mathcal Y,m}$; the covers of the sequence site are vertical, so its sheafified tensor with a system $N$ is levelwise, $(B_{\mathcal Y,m}\otimes_{B_{\mathcal Y,n}}Q)\otimes_{B_{\mathcal Y,m}}N_m$ (zero for $m>n$), and acyclicity is levelwise [lem-pur-system-level-left-extension]. Hence $G_B$ of it is computed by termwise $u_m^*$. Inverse image preserves K-flat flat-term complexes [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-pullback-preserves-kflat], so $L_n^{\mathcal X}$ of $u_n^*Q$ is also computed by its ordinary singleton extension, and both sides compute on the same $Q$. The canonical pullback/tensor comparison [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback] therefore gives the comparison on the normalized universal derived functors. At level $n$, multiplication by $B_n$ makes $e_n^{\mathcal X}c_n$ the identity of $u_n^*Q$.

source.place: Tags 07A4 (lemma-pullback-tensor-product), 07A6 (lemma-adjoint), 0D6E (lemma-derived-pushforward-composition), and 0B56 (equation-projection-formula-map); evaluation argument uses Zheng Construction 4.1, printed p. 21.

proof.text:
For $V\in D(B_{\mathcal Y,n})$ and $Z\in D(B_{\mathcal X})$, compose the specified adjunctions and $c_n$:
$$\operatorname{Hom}(V,e_n^{\mathcal Y}P_BZ)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(G_BL_n^{\mathcal Y}V,Z)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(L_n^{\mathcal X}u_n^*V,Z)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(V,Ru_{*,A_n}e_n^{\mathcal X}Z).$$
The middle bijection uses $c_n^{-1}$. Thus these are the two right adjoints of canonically identified left adjoints; apply [det-sp-unique-right-adjoint] to their composite counits: the natural bijections give a natural isomorphism $\beta_{n,Z}:e_n^{\mathcal Y}P_BZ\xrightarrow{\sim}Ru_{*,A_n}e_n^{\mathcal X}Z$. Track the image of $1_{e_nP_BZ}$. The first inverse transpose is $\varepsilon^B_Z\circ G_B(\lambda_{P_BZ})$, where $\lambda:L_ne_n\to1$ is the singleton counit. Its level-$n$ component is $e_n\varepsilon^B_Z$, since $e_n\lambda=1$ and $e_nc_n=1$. Consequently
$$e_n^{\mathcal X}\varepsilon^B_Z=\varepsilon^{(n)}_{e_n^{\mathcal X}Z}\circ u_n^*(\beta_{n,Z}).$$
Here the Hom/counit formulas are [lem-weil-pbc-adjunction-of-natural-bijection] and the composite-adjunction formulas are [lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting]. This identifies the actual finite adjunction, including its counit, without evaluating any K-injective replacement.

proof.text: These are the derived restriction/direct-image comparisons stipulated in the statement. To check the normalization, let $r_{T,n}$ forget $B_{T,n}$ to $\underline A_T$. The diagram comparison $U_{\mathcal Y}P_B\cong P^JU_{\mathcal X}$ is [lem-pur-diagram-ring-restriction-pushforward]. The finite comparison $r_{\mathcal Y,n}Ru_{*,A_n}\cong P r_{\mathcal X,n}$ is [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pushforward-composition] applied to the two factorizations through the identity-topos coefficient maps. Combine these with [lem-weil-pbc-tower-derived-evaluation-normalization] on constant-$A$ towers. Their evaluation square has the same mate as $r_{\mathcal Y,n}\beta_n$: composing the singleton adjunction with scalar extension, its left side has components $u_m^*(B_m\otimes_{B_n}Q)$, and the other side has $B_m\otimes_{B_n}u_n^*Q$, exactly the maps of Step 2. The ordinary scalar transpose is $x\otimes b\mapsto b\,g(x)$ by [lem-pur-sheaf-ring-derived-coefficient-adjunction]. Thus the two pastings are equal by [lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting], not by assuming that scalar restriction or evaluation preserves K-injectives. This fixes the restriction/direct-image normalization of $\beta_n$.

source.place: Tags 07A4 (lemma-pullback-tensor-product), 07A6 (lemma-adjoint), 0D6E (lemma-derived-pushforward-composition), and 0B56 (equation-projection-formula-map); evaluation argument uses Zheng Construction 4.1, printed p. 21.

proof.text:
Evaluation of scalar extension is normalized by the actual quotient maps. Under the equivalences of [lem-weil-pbc-diagram-site-realization], $\Delta$ is the constant diagram: it is exact and levelwise the identity, and the constant ring diagram is $\Delta\underline A_T$. Let $Q$ be a flat-term K-flat representative of $V$. Then $\Delta Q$ is K-flat with flat terms over $\Delta\underline A_T$, and $\Delta Q\otimes_{\Delta\underline A_T}B_T=(Q\otimes_A\underline{A_m}_T)_m$ has levels that are K-flat with flat terms over $\underline{A_m}_T$ [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-pullback-preserves-kflat] (identity topos, ring map $A\to A_m$). Both statements follow because the diagram topology has vertical covers, so tensor products and acyclicity are levelwise, as in Step 2. Hence $\mathcal R_TV$ is represented by $(Q\otimes_A\underline{A_m}_T)_m$ and $e_n\mathcal R_TV=V\otimes_A^L\underline{A_n}_T$. The coefficient unit is $q\mapsto q\otimes1$ [lem-pur-sheaf-ring-derived-coefficient-adjunction]. Applying the tensor comparison of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback] to scalar extension and to evaluation gives
$$e_n\mathcal R_{\mathcal Y}M\cong(PH)_n\otimes^L_{A_n}K_n,\qquad e_n\mathcal R_{\mathcal X}N\cong H_n\otimes^L_{A_n}u_n^*K_n.$$
The balancing maps send $(x\otimes a)\otimes(y\otimes b)$ to $(x\otimes y)\otimes ab$, with the canonical total-complex convention; no quotient flatness is used.

proof.text:
Set $h_{H,n}=\beta_{n,\mathcal R_{\mathcal X}H}\circ e_n(h_H)$. The defining transpose identity for $h_H$ is
$$\varepsilon^B_{\mathcal R_{\mathcal X}H}\circ G_B(h_H)=S_{\mathcal X}\Delta(\varepsilon_H),$$
with the specified scalar/pullback identifications. Evaluate it and substitute the counit identity of Step 3. The result is
$$\varepsilon^{(n)}_{H_n}\circ u_n^*(h_{H,n})=(\varepsilon_H)\otimes_A^L1_{\underline{A_n}}.$$
Thus $h_{H,n}$ is precisely the evaluated coefficient mate, under the source identification of Step 5. This is the inverse-transpose formula of [lem-weil-pbc-adjunction-of-natural-bijection]; it uses the canonical tensor comparison, rather than any separately chosen adjunction.

source.place: Tags 07A4 (lemma-pullback-tensor-product), 07A6 (lemma-adjoint), 0D6E (lemma-derived-pushforward-composition), and 0B56 (equation-projection-formula-map); evaluation argument uses Zheng Construction 4.1, printed p. 21.

proof.text:
For arbitrary $Z\in D(B_{\mathcal X})$ and $W\in D(B_{\mathcal Y})$, evaluate the defining transpose of $\pi^B_{Z,W}$. The tensor comparison commutes with the evaluation square: apply [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-exchange-tensor-coherence] with $f=u_B$, $f'=u_n$, and $g,g'$ the two evaluation morphisms. Their exchange is exactly $\beta_n$ of Step 3, since its transpose is the evaluated counit. The result is
$$\beta_{n,Z\otimes^LG_BW}\circ e_n(\pi^B_{Z,W})=\pi^{(n)}_{e_nZ,e_nW}\circ(\beta_{n,Z}\otimes^L1_{e_nW}).$$
In particular the finite projection here is the adjunct of $\varepsilon^{(n)}\otimes1$, as required. The cited coherence theorem requires a commutative ringed square, not a cartesian square or invertibility of the projection transformation.

source.place: Tags 07A4 (lemma-pullback-tensor-product), 07A6 (lemma-adjoint), 0D6E (lemma-derived-pushforward-composition), and 0B56 (equation-projection-formula-map); evaluation argument uses Zheng Construction 4.1, printed p. 21.

proof.text:
Apply Step 7 with $Z=\mathcal R_{\mathcal X}H$ and $W=\mathcal R_{\mathcal Y}K$, and precompose with $e_n(h_H\otimes1)$. Exact evaluation is a functor, so it preserves this composition. Its canonical tensor comparison sends that precomposition to $e_n(h_H)\otimes1$. Step 6 replaces $\beta_n e_n(h_H)$ by $h_{H,n}$, while Step 5 balances source and target. Therefore
$$e_n(v)=\pi^{(n)}_{H_n,K_n}(h_{H,n}\otimes^L_{A_n}1_{K_n}),$$
with source $M_n\cong(PH)_n\otimes^L_{A_n}K_n$ and target $Ru_{*,A_n}(H_n\otimes^L_{A_n}u_n^*K_n)$. Naturality follows from the naturality of each factor.

source.place: Tags 07A4 (lemma-pullback-tensor-product), 07A6 (lemma-adjoint), 0D6E (lemma-derived-pushforward-composition), and 0B56 (equation-projection-formula-map); evaluation argument uses Zheng Construction 4.1, printed p. 21.

proof.text: Finally check the quotient transitions, rather than inferring an equality of system morphisms from unrelated evaluations. For $m\geq n$, [lem-pur-system-single-derived-evaluation] identifies $e_nL_m$ with $B_n\otimes^L_{B_m}(-)$ and identifies its Hom transpose with the actual $m$-to-$n$ system transition. Apply this identity to the Hom chain in Step 3. The comparison $c_m$ at level $n$ is the scalar pullback map of Step 2, so this chain intertwines the transition of $P_BZ$ with $Ru_{*,A_m}$ of the transition of $Z$, followed by the canonical coefficient-restriction/direct-image comparison of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pushforward-composition]. Thus $\beta_m,\beta_n$ commute with the restriction-form transitions. The scalar tensor maps in Step 5 commute with those transitions because both orders send $(x\otimes a)\otimes(y\otimes b)$ to $(x\otimes y)\otimes\bar a\bar b$ after quotienting. Apply these facts to the single system maps $h_H$, $\varepsilon^B$, and $\pi_B$, so Steps 6--8 are compatible with every quotient transition. At $m=n$ all these maps are identities. The argument uses neither perfectness nor completion, and nowhere asserts preservation of K-injectives by varying-ring evaluation.
